passage:
Sahil: you don't get it!!
Keerthana: I DO get it, you promised you'd come
Sahil: I said maybe
Keerthana: you said yes 😠
Sahil: STOP SHOUTING
Keerthana: I'm not shouting, I'm typing in capitals because I'm so hurt
Sahil: ...
Keerthana: ok that came out louder than I meant. can we take ten minutes and then talk properly?
Sahil: yes
Sahil: I'm sorry I said maybe when I meant no
Sahil: I didn't want to say no to your face
Keerthana: thanks for saying it. I'd rather hear a no than get a maybe. I wanted you there. that's really all it was 🙂

qa.q: What did Keerthana say Sahil had promised?
qa.a: Keerthana said Sahil had promised to come.

qa.q: What was Keerthana feeling behind the capitals and anger?
qa.a: Keerthana was hurt and wanted Sahil there, and said that was all it was. The later softer tone shows the anger came from hurt.

qa.q: What worked when Keerthana changed approach?
qa.a: Keerthana noticed it came out too loud, asked for a short break and suggested talking properly. Taking a break and lowering the voice worked better than escalating.

qa.q: How might Sahil have felt when Keerthana yelled?
qa.a: Sahil probably felt attacked and defensive, which is why Sahil told Keerthana to stop shouting. Sahil later apologised for saying maybe.

grounding: A teenager yells in a quarrel from hurt, then takes a break and returns to talk more calmly.

passage: The bus to the fair at Kasba was late, and Nikita's brother Gautam had left without her again. She stormed into the courtyard. "You always do this!" she yelled. Gautam yelled back, "You're never ready!" Their grandmother looked out from the kitchen. Nikita's chest burned. She stopped, pressed her lips together, and walked to the well. She splashed water on her face, breathed slowly, and lowered her shoulders. When she came back, she said in a quieter voice, "I was really upset. I wanted to go with you." Gautam blinked. "I didn't know that. Next time I'll wait."

qa.q: Who looked out from the kitchen during the yelling?
qa.a: Their grandmother looked out from the kitchen.

qa.q: What was Nikita feeling when she yelled at Gautam?
qa.a: She was hurt and frustrated at being left behind, and wanted to be heard. She later said she really wanted to go with him.

qa.q: What could Nikita and Gautam do the next time a quarrel starts?
qa.a: Take a break, lower their voices and come back to talk, as Nikita did. That works better than yelling back.

qa.q: How might Gautam have felt when Nikita came back quieter?
qa.a: He seemed surprised and softened, since he hadn't known she wanted to go with him. He promised to wait.

grounding: A teenager yells from hurt in a quarrel, takes a break, lowers the voice and returns to talk.
